events.title: Magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes off Sarangani
events.detail: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake (PHIVOLCS) struck offshore approximately 25km southwest of Kablalan, Sarangani Province, at 07:37:41 AM PHT on June 8, 2026 (23:37:40 UTC June 7). USGS placed the depth at 57km; PHIVOLCS at 33km. Shaking lasted roughly 70 seconds and was felt across Mindanao. A tsunami warning was issued immediately for the southern Philippine coast.

events.title: Tsunami waves up to 2.5m strike southern Mindanao coast
events.detail: Tsunami waves reached a maximum run-up of 2.5 meters at Lebak, Sultan Kudarat; 1.48m along the Sarangani coast and 0.84m in Sultan Kudarat. Smaller waves (0.21-0.25m) were recorded at Zamboanga and Mati, Davao Oriental. The tsunami also reached Indonesia's North Sulawesi (up to ~1m), Palau, and Japan's Pacific coast (up to 30cm). Two people drowned in the Philippines and one remained missing.

events.title: Aftershock swarm tops 1,000 as death toll climbs
events.detail: PHIVOLCS recorded over 1,000 aftershocks by 7am June 9, with two reaching magnitude 6.5. The Philippine death toll rose past 32 with more than 100 injured as rescue teams worked through collapsed buildings in General Santos, Malapatan and Glan.

events.title: DSWD deploys 1.1 million pre-positioned food packs, cash aid pledged
events.detail: Secretary Rex Gatchalian flew to Mindanao as DSWD released over 1.1 million pre-positioned family food packs. Officials acknowledged early relief was slowed because local government personnel expected to distribute aid were themselves earthquake victims. Cash aid payouts to affected families were set to begin June 23.

events.title: Marcos visits Mindanao, pledges ₱50,000 per quake death, orders swift rehab
events.detail: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. inspected the quake-hit zone on June 10, pledging ₱50,000 to each family that lost a member and ordering agencies to expedite rehabilitation, price freezes and tax deadline extensions for affected areas.

events.title: VP Duterte visits earthquake victims in Malapatan and General Santos
events.detail: Vice President Sara Duterte visited earthquake-affected families in Malapatan, Sarangani and General Santos City, deploying a food truck to prepare hot meals for first responders working collapsed-building rescues, and distributing food and non-food aid to displaced residents.

events.title: PHIVOLCS documents up to 2m of coastal uplift over 100km
events.detail: PHIVOLCS confirmed the Cotabato Trench rupture raised the coastline by as much as 2 meters along roughly 100km of Sarangani and Davao Occidental shoreline, exposing coral reefs and stranding fishing boats — contributing to an estimated ₱70 billion in marine resource damage.

events.title: Aftershocks pass 8,500; Solidum warns Metro Manila also at risk
events.detail: PHIVOLCS Director Renato Solidum Jr. said aftershocks had passed 8,500 as of mid-August and reiterated that a magnitude 7.2 'Big One' remains possible on Metro Manila's West Valley Fault, urging nationwide earthquake preparedness independent of the Mindanao sequence.

events.title: DBM releases initial ₱362 million for Mindanao rehabilitation
events.detail: The Department of Budget and Management released an initial ₱362 million to rehabilitate public facilities — schools, health centers, roads — damaged by the M7.8 earthquake, as Congress began drafting a larger supplemental rehabilitation package.

events.title: Typhoon Bavi forms east-southeast of Kwajalein
events.detail: A tropical disturbance east-southeast of Kwajalein organized into a tropical depression on June 30, 2026, and was named Bavi by JMA on July 2 as it tracked northwest toward the Mariana Islands.

events.title: Pandaw landslide kills 10 in earthquake-weakened Malapatan, Sarangani
events.detail: Heavy rains from Bavi's outer bands, compounded by soil already destabilized by the June earthquake, triggered a landslide in Barangay Pandaw, Malapatan, Sarangani, killing 10 people — the deadliest single landslide of the Bavi-enhanced monsoon episode.

events.title: Calanogas landslide kills 7, state of calamity declared
events.detail: A landslide attributed to Bavi's rains killed 7 people, injured 2 and left 4 missing in Calanogas, Lanao del Sur. The municipality subsequently declared a state of calamity to unlock emergency funds.

events.title: Bukidnon landslide kills 3, leaves 3 missing
events.detail: A separate Bavi-triggered landslide in Bukidnon province killed 3 people, injured 5 and left 3 missing, part of a broader pattern of slope failures across earthquake-weakened Mindanao terrain.

events.title: Bavi makes landfall in eastern China as super typhoon
events.detail: After peaking at 285km/h (JTWC 1-minute sustained) and grazing Taiwan, Bavi made landfall near Yuhuan, Zhejiang, around 15:20 UTC on July 11, prompting China's flood control authority to raise its emergency response to Level II for Zhejiang and Fujian.

events.title: Bavi dissipates; Philippine toll reaches 23+ dead, 782,874 affected
events.detail: Typhoon Bavi (locally Inday) dissipated July 16 after affecting the Marianas, Philippines, Taiwan and China. In the Philippines it left 23+ dead, 14+ missing, 163+ injured, damaged 1,202 houses and 41 infrastructure facilities, and directly affected 782,874 people, of whom 24,000 were displaced.

events.title: Marcos declares national energy emergency after Strait of Hormuz closure
events.detail: Following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the 2026 Iran war — which disrupted roughly 20% of global oil supply and hit the Philippines especially hard given its 98% Middle East oil import dependence — President Marcos signed Executive Order 110 declaring a state of national energy emergency on March 24, 2026, making the Philippines the first nation to do so in response to the war. The crisis set the stage for the rolling blackouts that compounded the June-August disaster cascade.

events.title: Luzon and Visayas grids hit red alert, rotational brownouts begin
events.detail: NGCP placed the Luzon grid on red alert and the Visayas grid on yellow-to-red alert on May 13-15 after transmission line trips disconnected over 2,400MW of gas-fired capacity, triggering 2-3 hour rotational brownouts affecting nearly 2 million consumers. Visayan Electric implemented one-hour rotational brownouts in Cebu on May 13 under the same grid emergency.

events.title: DOE orders full technical review of NGCP after blackout scale draws fire
events.detail: Energy Secretary Sharon Garin ordered NGCP and generators to restore normal grid conditions and demanded 'full technical disclosure, clear accountability, and immediate corrective action,' as lawmakers accused NGCP of blaming reporting delays rather than acknowledging a genuine supply shortfall.

events.title: Meralco pushes back after Marcos SONA call to reform system loss charges
events.detail: After President Marcos used his SONA to call on Congress to amend EPIRA and stop utilities passing system-loss charges and VAT onto consumers, Meralco warned such reforms could threaten utility operations and long-term infrastructure planning, deepening the standoff over blackout accountability heading into the August typhoon sequence.

events.title: NGCP issues Visayas yellow alert amid 797.6MW forced plant outages
events.detail: NGCP placed the Visayas grid under a yellow alert from 5-9pm on August 21 as peak demand of 2,444MW pressed against just 2,584MW of available capacity, with 28 power plants on forced outage and 14 running at derated capacity (including both Therma Visayas units) for a combined 797.6MW unavailable — the latest in a recurring string of red/yellow alerts through the disaster cascade, with the March 2026 national energy emergency under EO 110 still in effect.
events.confidenceReason: Single Tier-2 source reporting a routine NGCP grid-alert announcement; no independent corroboration found for this specific date.

events.title: M6.3 aftershock rattles crowd at Mindanao cash-subsidy site
events.detail: A magnitude 6.3 aftershock struck Mindanao on August 5, two months into recovery, while displaced survivors were gathered to receive cash subsidies — underscoring President Marcos's earlier caution that full rebuilding could not proceed while the aftershock sequence continued.

events.title: Congress seeks ₱15 billion supplemental fund for Mindanao rehabilitation
events.detail: With nearly 113,300 homes damaged or destroyed across Mindanao by the earthquake and aftershocks (18,300+ totally destroyed), Congress convened a special session to fast-track a ₱15 billion supplemental rehabilitation fund, with Senate President Pro Tempore Kiko Pangilinan citing Mindanao's role as the country's food basket.

events.title: Sarangani turns to private donors after DepEd funding shortfall for 1,500+ classrooms
events.detail: Sarangani's governor said the province would rely on private cash donations to repair over 1,500 damaged classrooms after the Department of Education acknowledged it lacked sufficient funds to cover all earthquake school repairs.

events.title: Tropical Depression Luis forms, PH's 12th cyclone of 2026
events.detail: Tropical Depression Luis formed with 55km/h winds on August 2, becoming the Philippines' 12th tropical cyclone of 2026 and the first of August, opening a sequence of storms that would compound the still-unresolved earthquake and energy crises.

events.title: Tropical Cyclone Kujira forms, triggers first flash update
events.detail: Tropical Cyclone Kujira developed and prompted a ReliefWeb flash update on August 5, joining Luis and the approaching Maymay in a cluster of systems that would combine with the southwest monsoon to inundate Luzon through mid-August.

events.title: Tropical Storm Maymay makes landfall in Ilocos Sur
events.detail: Tropical Storm Maymay, the Philippines' 13th cyclone of 2026, made landfall in Ilocos Sur early on August 6 with maximum sustained winds of 75km/h, before weakening and exiting via Isabela the following day.

events.title: Super Typhoon Dolphin reaches Category 5 strength, enhances habagat
events.detail: Typhoon Dolphin intensified into a Category 5 super typhoon with sustained winds exceeding 257km/h — the fifth Cat-5 storm of the 2026 Pacific season. While tracking well offshore northeast of Luzon, it dramatically enhanced the southwest monsoon (habagat) rains over the Philippines rather than making a direct landfall, injuring 6 people in Japan's Okinawa and Kagoshima as its outer bands passed.

events.title: Habagat/typhoon death toll opens at 6, hundreds of thousands affected
events.detail: NDRRMC's first consolidated tally on August 9 put deaths from the enhanced habagat and tropical cyclones Luis and Maymay at 6, with more than 382,000 people and 110,000 families affected across Luzon and the Visayas.

events.title: Baguio landslide in Barangay Guisad kills 10, Metro Manila classes suspended
events.detail: A landslide in Barangay Guisad, Baguio City, Benguet, killed 10 residents as heavy habagat rains continued. Malacañang suspended face-to-face classes and in-person government work across Metro Manila and 15 provinces on August 10 amid the flooding.

events.title: Death toll rises to 19 as 2.27 million people affected
events.detail: By August 11, NDRRMC reported the combined death toll from storms and the southwest monsoon had risen to 19, with 2.27 million people affected across Luzon and the Visayas and thousands sheltering in evacuation centers.

events.title: Death toll climbs to 21 as rains persist
events.detail: NDRRMC's August 15 update put the death toll from the storm-and-monsoon sequence at 21, with continued flooding and landslide risk keeping thousands in evacuation centers across Luzon and the Cordilleras.

events.title: Death toll reaches 26; 5.1 million Filipinos affected by combined storm sequence
events.detail: By August 18, NDRRMC put the combined death toll from the enhanced southwest monsoon, Tropical Depression Luis and Tropical Cyclone Kujira at 26 — with Benguet (15 deaths, largely the Guisad landslide), Rizal (3) and Batangas (3) hardest hit — and 5.1 million people affected. Infrastructure damage reached ₱2.647 billion and agricultural losses ₱347.37 million.

events.title: IFRC warns humanitarian resources 'dwindling' as needs from cascade soar
events.detail: IFRC Head of Delegation for the Philippines Sanjeev Kafley warned that 'humanitarian needs are soaring, but resources are dwindling' as the Philippine Red Cross and IFRC stretched to cover overlapping earthquake, typhoon and monsoon response operations simultaneously across Mindanao and Luzon.

events.title: Tropical Depression Neneng forms, PH's 14th cyclone of 2026
events.detail: Tropical Depression Neneng developed from a low-pressure area east of the country on August 18, becoming the Philippines' 14th tropical cyclone of 2026. PAGASA said Neneng was unlikely to make direct landfall but would track northwest toward Taiwan while pulling in and enhancing the southwest monsoon over Luzon and the Visayas, prolonging the habagat rains through the following week.

media.caption: PAGASA tropical cyclone track map showing newly formed Tropical Depression Neneng

events.title: Marcos unveils plan for underground cisterns at 30 Metro Manila sites
events.detail: President Marcos announced on the evening of August 19, during a briefing at the MMDA command center, that the government had identified 30 potential sites in Metro Manila — including Rajah Sulayman, Rizal Memorial, Camp Aguinaldo and the University of Santo Tomas — to build underground cisterns storing floodwater beneath existing facilities, with help from Dutch flood-control experts. Detailed engineering was expected within the month, positioning the cisterns as a long-term mitigation measure after repeated habagat flooding of the capital.

media.caption: Flooded Gumamela Street, Quezon City, amid habagat rains that prompted the underground cistern plan

events.title: Death toll climbs to 29 as 6.5 million affected, infrastructure damage hits ₱4.66 billion
events.detail: The Office of Civil Defense's August 20 report put the combined death toll from the enhanced habagat and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng at 29, with 19 injured and 3 missing. Over 6.5 million individuals (1.8 million+ families) were affected, 47,277 people remained in evacuation centers, 40 landslide incidents were recorded across Ilocos, CAR, CALABARZON and MIMAROPA, and infrastructure damage reached ₱4.66 billion across 1,013 sites. Agricultural losses climbed to ₱1.73 billion as of August 21, per the Department of Agriculture.

media.caption: Philippine Coast Guard rescue operation amid habagat and Neneng-enhanced flooding

events.title: 88 cities and municipalities — including four entire provinces — declared under state of calamity
events.detail: NDRRMC Executive Director Undersecretary Harold Cabreros confirmed 88 cities and municipalities nationwide, including the entire provinces of Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga and Cavite plus localities in Pangasinan, Zambales, Rizal and Batangas, had been placed under a state of calamity due to the habagat and cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng as of August 21. The declarations unlock emergency funds and price controls and follow Memorandum No. 214, s. 2026 directing agencies to prioritize the most vulnerable affected populations.

media.caption: Flooded Baguio City landslide rescue operation amid the widening habagat state-of-calamity declarations

events.title: 102 areas now under state of calamity as 7.5 million affected by habagat and cyclone sequence
events.detail: OCD/NDRRMC reports through August 24 put the number of local government units under a state of calamity at 102 across 12 provinces and cities — including Dagupan, Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro — up from 88-89 in the preceding days. The death toll held at 29 (19 injured, 3 missing) even as the affected population grew to roughly 7.5 million people (2.2 million families) across 10 regions, with 418 evacuation centers sheltering 33,358 people. Infrastructure losses climbed to ₱5.1 billion and agricultural damage held near ₱1.7 billion.

media.caption: Flood-hit communities as NDRRMC widens state-of-calamity coverage to over 100 local government units

events.title: Entire Benguet province placed under state of calamity as cumulative damage tops ₱1 billion
events.detail: The Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Benguet declared the entire province under a state of calamity on August 24, following weeks of heavy rain, landslides and damaged roads linked to the Luis-Maymay-Neneng-Dolphin-Kujira sequence and the enhanced habagat. A partial assessment by the Benguet Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office put cumulative damage at ₱1.068 billion (₱749.89 million infrastructure, ₱318.64 million agriculture), affecting 40,121 people across 13,031 families. The declaration unlocks ₱38 million from the province's Quick Response Fund and follows a narrower August 18 state-of-calamity declaration for provincial capital La Trinidad, where infrastructure damage alone reached ₱57 million.

media.caption: Landslide-damaged roads in Benguet province amid the cumulative habagat and typhoon-sequence toll that triggered an Aug. 24 province-wide state-of-calamity declaration

events.title: Typhoon Obet (Saudel) briefly crosses PAR, further enhancing the habagat monsoon
events.detail: Typhoon Saudel, locally named Obet, entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility at 1:20 p.m. on August 24 as the country's 15th tropical cyclone of 2026, tracking roughly 1,350km east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon with sustained winds of 165km/h and gusts to 205km/h. PAGASA said Obet would remain over the Philippine Sea without direct landfall and it exited PAR around 9:30 p.m. the same day after nearing near-super-typhoon intensity. PAGASA weather specialist Grace Castañeda-Carpio said Obet's track near PAR's northern boundary would continue enhancing the southwest monsoon, bringing scattered rain and thunderstorms to Metro Manila, Ilocos, CAR, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Cavite, Batangas and Rizal into August 25, while the storm continued west-northwest toward southern Japan and, by August 28, mainland China's coast.

media.caption: Satellite tracking graphic for Typhoon Obet (Saudel) as it briefly transited the Philippine Area of Responsibility on August 24

events.title: Death toll climbs to 31 as 104 areas under state of calamity, infrastructure damage nears ₱6 billion
events.detail: NDRRMC's August 27 report (as of 6am) put the combined death toll from the enhanced habagat and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng at 31, up from 29. Regional breakdown: Benguet 15 (10 in Baguio City, 3 in Atok, 2 in La Trinidad, all landslide-related), CALABARZON 8 (4 Rizal, 4 Batangas), Metro Manila 3 (2 Caloocan, 1 Quezon City), and 5 more across La Union, Oriental Mindoro, Occidental Mindoro and Negros Occidental. 19 remained injured and 3 missing (Manila, Quezon City, Batangas City). The number of localities under a state of calamity grew to 104, infrastructure damage reached ₱5.95 billion, agricultural losses hit ₱1.91 billion, and more than 2,800 houses were damaged (2,500 partially, 340 totally destroyed). The affected population rose to 7.7 million people (2.2 million families) across 10 regions, while evacuation-center numbers fell to roughly 28,000 people (325 centers, 8,200 families) as floodwaters receded in some areas even as fresh orange rainfall warnings hit Zambales and Bataan the same evening.

media.caption: Flood debris in Parañaque as NDRRMC reports the death toll climbing to 31 and 104 areas under state of calamity
